newsitem.title: USA: State Street revenue, expenses up in Q4.
newsitem.headline: State Street revenue, expenses up in Q4.

text.p: State Street Boston Corp said its fourth-quarter revenue jumped 20 percent from a year ago to $501 million, reflecting growth in fiduciary compensation and net interest revenue.
Operating expenses for the fourth quarter rose 21 percent to $375 million, reflecting support of business growth, it said.
Salaries and employee benefits rose 20 percent to $211 million due to additional staff, incentive compensation and salary increases, it said.

State Street said fiduciary compensation, derived from accounting, custody, recordkeeping, information, investment management and trustee services, was up 20 percent to $270 million. It said the rise was due to new business, customers' growth and asset appreciation.
In the financial asset servicing business, strong revenue growth from accounting and custody for mutual funds reflected a 28 percent increase in assets, the company said.
Outside the U.S., revenue grew rapidly and assets under custody rose 33 percent, State Street said.
For the fourth quarter, State Street said net income rose 20 percent to $78 million. Earnings per share fully diluted rose 22 percent to $0.95.
Average shares outstanding on a fully diluted basis declined to 82 millon in the quarter from 84 million a year ago.
According to Institutional Brokers Estimate System, the range of Wall Street estimates for State Street's fourth quarter earnings was $0.90 to $0.93 per share, and the mean was $0.92.
State Street shares were off 1/8 at 70-1/4 in morning trade.
